transcript:
Summary: quick alignment on Private deployment footprint, perf expectations, security checklist, and pilot next steps. Topics: Private (VPC) deployment, KMS/HSM key mgmt, SSO/SCIM, audit logs, rollout and canary plan, perf benchmark plan.

00:00 Avery Chen: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. this is Avery from Redwood. um, quick roll call.
00:06 Marta Lopez: Marta here — head of platform at Helix. good to see you all.
00:09 Ethan Cole: Ethan, SRE.
00:11 Priya Nair: Priya, security.
00:13 Ravi Patel: Ravi from Redwood, SE — I'll run the perf stuff.
00:16 Samir Khatri: Samir, DevOps.
00:18 Avery Chen: Awesome. Goal for today is to align on the pilot runway, surface any blockers, and agree next steps.

01:05 Marta Lopez: To give context — we have an internal microservice that will call the model for code-assist and also a customer-facing assistant. We're trying to decide whether to start on Hosted or go straight to Private.
01:28 Avery Chen: yeah. totally fair. from what we saw in the intake your compliance team prefers Private because of data residency and audit controls, right?
01:35 Priya Nair: Correct. We need SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logging, and KMS integration for keys. Also retention policies — we can't keep raw transcripts longer than 30 days.
01:46 Avery Chen: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and you can configure retention at route level, we'll share the policy knobs.
01:58 Ethan Cole: One thing — latency. Our SLAs target tail latency under 120ms for 256-token calls. we're worried about network spikes over VPC peering.
02:12 Ravi Patel: Good flag. For Private we typically co-locate inference nodes in the same cloud region; we also have Dedicated pools for predictable throughput. the perf harness we'll run emulates your token distribution so we can confirm tail percentiles.
02:30 Marta Lopez: can you clarify Dedicated vs Private? we thought Dedicated reserved capacity was a separate SKU.
02:36 Avery Chen: Sure — Private is the deployment mode with your control plane in a customer VPC; Dedicated is reserved capacity concept — you can have Dedicated capacity inside Private (i.e., reserved GPU pools in your VPC) or use Hosted Dedicated where we provision dedicated nodes in our managed environment.
02:54 Priya Nair: ok that helped. also, what's the KV cache behavior — do you keep long lived KV caches in-memory or is there persistence? we have bursty workloads and caching matters for cost.
03:08 Ravi Patel: It's an in-memory KV cache at the runtime; we do prefix caching and cache warm-up. sometimes the transcript output transcriber shows it as K-V cash, haha, but it's in-memory only. there's also a persistent checkpoint for cold-start recovery but not a long-lived token store.
03:26 Samir Khatri: That makes sense. For our side we'll want to test cold-start on scale-up events. can the autoscaler do step scaling for GPU fleets?
03:36 Ravi Patel: yes — autoscaling supports step and scheduled policies. we can show you our suggested policy based on your traffic curve.

05:00 Marta Lopez: timeline question: We're aiming for a pilot starting mid-June, 4 weeks long. success criteria: 1) latency SLOs met for 95th and 99th, 2) integration with SSO and KMS, 3) no P0 security findings. is that reasonable?
05:22 Avery Chen: Totally reasonable. we'll run a perf week in week 1 and then a feature/ops validation week.
05:28 Priya Nair: Security-wise, we'll need the SOC2 artifact + ISO put into our vendor onboarding. also a list of controls around key access.
05:36 Avery Chen: We'll send the latest SOC2 report and our security pack. Our security engineer can jump on a follow-up if you want a deeper walkthrough.

07:10 Ethan Cole: on the perf bench — our real traffic has a bimodal distribution: quick 16–32 token queries (embedding lookups) and 400–800 tokens for code explainers. can you run both profiles?
07:26 Ravi Patel: Absolutely. we'll create two load profiles and a mixed profile. for the code explainer runs we'll test 512 and 1024 token truncations too.

08:45 Marta Lopez: one blocker for us historically has been SSO provisioning — SCIM sync took weeks before; what's your experience?
08:55 Avery Chen: SCIM mostly works out of the box with common IdPs; small mapping quirks can slow things. we usually recommend a staging SCIM sync with a small set of test users first.
09:08 Priya Nair: Do you support just-in-time provisioning?
09:11 Ravi Patel: We support both SCIM and JIT for some IdPs. we'll share the exact list in the security doc.

11:00 Samir Khatri: network requirements — what's the egress IPs we need to allow?
11:06 Avery Chen: For Private in your VPC there are no public egress requirements; for Hosted there are a set of IPs. we'll give you the Private peering and firewall checklist.
11:15 Samir Khatri: Great.

12:40 Marta Lopez: cost — high level. we need to show finance a rough monthly run rate for pilot and for 99th percentile load.
12:48 Avery Chen: We'll share a ballpark based on your token mix and projected concurrent users. Redwood Optimize will also give quantization and batching suggestions to reduce unit costs.
12:59 Ethan Cole: Are there any hard limits on model size or custom model imports with Private? We may want to bring an internally tuned LLM later.
13:09 Ravi Patel: Private supports custom model artifacts if they fit supported architectures; there are packaging and validation steps. we'll send the model-onboarding checklist.

15:30 Marta Lopez: on rollouts — we want canary and gradual traffic ramp with automatic fallback to a smaller model on errors. is that supported?
15:39 Avery Chen: Yes — Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies by route. you can configure a fallback to a lower-cost variant on error or high latency.
15:51 Priya Nair: Audit logs — do logs include token-level traces or only request/response metadata?
15:58 Ravi Patel: We capture request metadata, timestamps, route/model version, and limited token-level metrics for cost accounting; raw user content retention is a configurable setting to meet privacy needs.

18:00 Marta Lopez: ok if we outline the golden prompt set and a traffic sample, how fast can you spin up a staging environment?
18:08 Avery Chen: Once we have peering details and a small VM/account access for staging, we can provision a staging stack within 72 hours, then run validations.
18:16 Samir Khatri: we'll need an infra ticket; I'll put that in our backlog after this call.

20:00 Ethan Cole: mixing in a couple of nitty-gritty things — tokenization differences across models, prompt truncation behavior, and how embeddings are versioned.
20:10 Ravi Patel: Good pickup — different model families have different tokenizers; we'll give you a mapping and the best practice of adding a thin normalization layer to harmonize token counts. embeddings are versioned per model artifact; you'll get model-id and artifact hash in the response.

22:30 Marta Lopez: Any red flags from your side?
22:33 Avery Chen: The two things to watch: (1) network peering/firewall rules not applied in time can delay the staging spin-up; (2) SCIM mapping quirks can slow SSO validation. both are mitigated by staging test users and early firewall rule prod prep.

25:00 Priya Nair: on key mgmt — rotation cadence. Do you allow customer-initiated key rotation without downtime?
25:08 Ravi Patel: You can rotate keys; there's a rollover process that supports overlapping keys so you shouldn't have downtime if you follow the runbook. we'll share the key rotation steps.

27:00 Marta Lopez: Let's lock dates: perf bench week of 6/14, staging provision by 6/12, pilot start 6/21 for 4 weeks.
27:12 Avery Chen: Sounds good. we'll commit to sending architecture + security docs by 6/11.

30:00 Samir Khatri: Quick question — are there any special kernel optimizations we should expect if we're running on NVIDIA A100 vs H100?
30:08 Ravi Patel: Yes, kernel selection and quantization paths change; H100 has different matrix core characteristics. we'll include a short note in the model onboarding doc that explains recommended instance types and quantization picks.

33:50 Marta Lopez: ok last mile — who owns the pilot success sign-off?
33:55 Ethan Cole: From Helix, final sign-off will be a joint decision by Platform (Marta) and Security (Priya).
34:02 Priya Nair: We'll sign off after a security review and one week of stable operations in staging.
34:07 Avery Chen: Great — on Redwood side we'll provide a checklist and label owners.

37:20 Ravi Patel: I'll prepare the perf harness and a shared spreadsheet to capture the results: p50/p95/p99, token counts, throughput, cost per 1M tokens.
37:29 Marta Lopez: please include variability metrics and a note on cold starts.
37:33 Ravi Patel: Will do.

40:00 Avery Chen: Recap: send security pack + architecture (Avery) by 6/11, Ravi will schedule perf bench and deliver harness by 6/14, Helix to send golden prompts + traffic sample by 6/12, Samir to provision staging network by 6/13.
40:20 Marta Lopez: That works. Also, can you share an example runbook for incident response during pilot?
40:26 Avery Chen: Yes — we'll include an incident runbook and escalation path in the doc bundle.

42:10 Priya Nair: small note — please redact any PII in logs by default; we need an explicit opt-in for full content retention.
42:18 Avery Chen: Affirmative. default will be metadata-only retention unless you opt in.

44:00 Marta Lopez: Thanks everyone. we'll loop back after we get the docs.
44:05 Ethan Cole: Thanks.
44:07 Ravi Patel: Thanks y'all.
44:09 Avery Chen: Bye.
44:12 [meeting ends]
